property_summary: For any inputs the reference contract's transfer(...) call always completes successfully (returns true) regardless of the callee reverting/non-reverting, because it uses low-level call which returns success for external non-reverting fallbacks; replacing call with staticcall can make transfer(...) return differently (fail) when the callee's fallback rejects state-less static calls — the mutant can thus cause transfer to return false for some callee behaviours that the reference tolerated.

For any callee contract that rejects static calls (i.e., its fallback reverts on staticcall) and any non-empty arrays, the reference C always returns true from transfer (because it uses call), whereas the mutant using staticcall may return false for such callees, so the property is that transfer(...) returns true for all admissible inputs.

For any non-empty _tos/_v arrays and any from/caddress, C.transfer(...) always completes successfully and returns true (its low-level call ignores callee static-call restrictions), whereas the mutant using staticcall can cause transfer(...) to return false when the callee's fallback rejects static calls — so the property is that transfer(...) never fails (returns true) for all admissible inputs, which the mutant violates for some adversarial callee.
